title: Sierra Bank - Data Residency & Compliance Discovery
summary: Discovery focused on Sierra Bank's regulatory constraints for LLM usage: EU data residency for certain products, HIPAA adjacency for health-related customer interactions, PCI considerations, and strict logging/retention rules. Discussed tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments; Redwood AE/SE committed to share SOC2/HIPAA docs, EU-hosting options, and a pilot plan for a Dedicated instance with limited logging and KMS integration.

transcript:
[00:00] Alicia: Hey everybody, thanks for joining, I'm Alicia with Redwood, and with me is Daniel from our SE team. quick sound check?
[00:06] Laura: Yeah hi this is Laura, CISO at Sierra Bank, we can hear you.
[00:09] Mark: Mark here, infrastructure, good to meet you.
[00:11] Priya: Priya, compliance. thanks for setting this up.
[00:14] Alicia: Great, appreciate it. The goal today is to understand your residency and compliance constraints so we can recommend Hosted, Dedicated, or Private. can you walk us through the must-haves?
[00:24] Laura: Sure. high level — we have a couple of product lines that must keep data in the EU, others can be US. also we have health-adjacent customer support interactions used for triage that could touch PHI, so HIPAA concerns. and of course PCI cardholder data scope is strict for payments. We need auditability, tamper-evident logs, and controlled retention.
[00:40] Daniel: thanks Laura. when you say must keep in EU, is that at rest, in transit, or both? and do you need processing to occur in-region?
[00:48] Laura: Processing as well. Controllers in several countries insist that processing stay in EU datacenters. so both rest and processing. encryption alone doesn't cut it for them.
[00:57] Priya: also retention rules: certain logs cannot be stored more than 30 days, and some datasets we can't log at all. so we need a path to disable or filter request/response logging for those flows.
[01:07] Mark: Our stack is a mix of cloud and colocation; we prefer customer-managed networking (VPC peering) for anything that touches sensitive data.
[01:13] Alicia: got it. that's pretty common. here's how Redwood maps to those needs at a high level: Hosted gives you fastest time to market but logs and telemetry are in our hosted control plane; Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools and VPC options with stronger isolation and the ability to limit telemetry; Private gives you a customer-managed control plane for full tenancy and on-prem options.
[01:29] Alicia: do you currently use any managed LLM providers?
[01:32] Laura: we've done proofs with OpenAI and Azure OpenAI, but the compliance folks pushed back on broad telemetry and EU processing. we like the performance though.
[01:40] Daniel: okay thanks. for the flows that must process in EU, Redwood supports EU-hosted clusters and Dedicated instances in EU regions. we can also work with Private deployments if you need the control plane inside your network.
[01:51] Priya: about HIPAA — we need BAA and proof of safeguards. do you have experience in financial services handling PHI-adjacent data?
[01:58] Alicia: yes, we have customers in regulated sectors; we can provide SOC2 reports and HIPAA attestation where applicable, and we do KMS integrations so keys can be customer-managed.
[02:06] Laura: can you confirm whether we can prevent request/response logging for specific routes? that's a blocker for some of our use cases.
[02:12] Daniel: short answer — yes, with Dedicated and Private you get much finer control. for Hosted, we have limited options: you can mask or redact fields at the SDK level and use client-side filtering; but we don't currently offer per-route absolute no-logging for hosted tenants. Also note that some observability traces remain in control plane for debugging unless explicitly disabled.
[02:30] Priya: hm, that might be an issue. what about encryption and KMS — can we bring our own key?
[02:35] Alicia: yes, BYOK via KMS/HSM is supported for Dedicated and Private. for Hosted we offer platform-managed encryption but we can sign agreements around key management in some enterprise contracts.
[02:45] Mark: network topology — we need to see how VPC peering would look, and whether traffic ever leaves our VPC for model execution.
[02:52] Daniel: good question. for Dedicated we run the inference runtime in customer-dedicated pools; networking can be configured so model traffic stays within your peered VPC and egress is controlled. for Private we deploy inside your network so nothing leaves. for hosted there is always some control plane traffic to our hosted region.
[03:10] Laura: compliance wants immutable audit logs for access to keys and model versions. do you provide that?
[03:16] Alicia: yes, we provide audit trails; with Dedicated/Private you can forward logs to your SIEM and keep retention policies. we can show examples in the security pack.
[03:24] Priya: PCI — any concerns about cardholder data touching the model? we would want to ensure tokenization or redaction before it hits inference.
[03:30] Daniel: absolutely. recommended pattern is client-side tokenization or deterministic redaction. we can also put a pre-processing proxy to scrub PHI/PCI fields before hitting the model. we have customers using that approach.
[03:42] Mark: performance — if we go Dedicated in EU with stricter logging and KMS calls, what's the latency impact?
[03:48] Daniel: adding KMS on the critical path can add tens to low hundreds of ms depending on HSM setup; we avoid per-token KMS calls by caching keys in the runtime and using envelope encryption. Dedicated GPUs and local region placement minimize network latency. we can run a benchmark pilot to quantify.
[04:04] Laura: timeline — we need something in production-ish in Q2 next year, pilot in Q1. is that realistic?
[04:10] Alicia: yes, that aligns. typical flow: pilot (4–8 weeks) -> canary -> production. for Dedicated the procurement and capacity reservation can take longer, but we'll work the timelines with you.
[04:20] Priya: one more — data subject rights under GDPR. we need the ability to delete logs and their associated artifacts on request. is that supported?
[04:27] Daniel: yes, we provide deletion APIs and for Dedicated/Private you control retention. for Hosted we have processes but you'll want contractual SLAs for data deletion which we can provide.
[04:36] Mark: can you also confirm where model weights sit? some vendors insist model weights cannot leave provider network.
[04:41] Alicia: model weights for our curated open models are stored in the region where you deploy. for Private we can deploy customized weights inside your environment. if there are export restrictions we'll need to validate per-model.
[04:52] Priya: anything else we should know?
[04:55] Alicia: we'll send the security pack, including SOC2, HIPAA attestation, encryption docs, sample VPC architecture, and a proposed pilot plan. We'll also include a short benchmark spreadsheet so you can see expected latency/cost with Dedicated EU nodes.
[05:07] Laura: please also include sample contracts for BAA and data processing addenda.
[05:11] Alicia: noted.
[05:12] Priya: thanks.
[05:13] Alicia: ok let's do a quick recap of next steps — Daniel, you take the lead on the Dedicated config and the pilot plan, Alicia will send the security docs, and Sierra will provide the list of sensitive endpoints.
[05:22] Daniel: sounds good.
[05:23] Mark: thanks all.
[05:24] Laura: thanks, bye.
[05:25] [call ended]
